title: Max Area of Island
statement: You get a grid of 0 (water) and 1 (land). An island is a group of land cells joined up, down, left or right. Its area is how many cells it has. Return the largest area of any island, or 0 if the grid has no land.

example.caption: Two islands, with areas 3 and 2. The answer is the bigger one, 3.

idea.sentence: Flood each island once and let the flood return how many cells it claimed: one for the current cell plus whatever its four neighbours add. Keep the largest total.

jargon.plain: Start at one cell and spread to every connected land cell, claiming each one so it is never visited twice.
The number of land cells in one island.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the map as rows of 0 and 1, e.g. [[1,1,0],[0,1,0]]

vars.meaning: number of cells in the map (rows times columns)

compare.bruteLabel: Flood from every land cell with a fresh visited set
compare.optimalLabel: Flood each island once, keep the claims

rows.name: Fresh flood per land cell
rows.note: Every land cell starts its own flood over its whole island, and the visited set is rebuilt each time.

rows.name: Claim cells and keep them
rows.note: Each cell is claimed once. Space is the owner grid plus the recursion depth, which can reach n.

fast.takeaway: Same as counting islands, with one change: the flood returns a number instead of nothing. Claimed cells stay claimed, so no cell is counted twice.

stages.title: Nothing claimed
stages.note: A grid of island numbers, all 0. A cell with 0 has no owner yet.

stages.title: New island found
stages.note: Land with no owner starts a new island. Give it the next number and flood from here.

stages.title: Flood and add up
stages.note: Claim the cell and return 1 plus what each of the four neighbours returns. Water, claimed cells and edges return 0.

stages.title: Keep the best
stages.note: After each flood, best becomes the larger of best and the new area. The result is best, 0 if no land.

edges.title: No land
edges.why: No flood starts, so best stays at its start value. Starting best at 0 gives the right answer.

edges.title: Everything is land
edges.why: One flood covers all nine cells. A wrong version that forgets to claim cells would loop or double count.

edges.title: Ring around water
edges.why: The flood goes round the ring. The water in the middle is not counted.

edges.title: Diagonal land
edges.why: Diagonals do not join. Each cell is its own island of area 1.

gotchas.text: new Array(rows).fill(new Array(cols).fill(0)) shares one inner array between all rows. Claiming a cell would then claim it in every row. Use Array.from({ length: rows }, () => new Array(cols).fill(0)).
Do not test land[r][c] for truthiness before checking the bounds. land[-1] is undefined, and undefined[c] throws. Check the bounds first, then the cell.
Each row of make([][]int, rows) starts nil. Allocate every row before the first write. The recursive closure needs var area func(r, c, id int) int declared before it is assigned.
Count the cell when you claim it, not when you look at it. If you add 1 before the claimed check, a cell reached from two sides is added twice.

recap.pattern: Flood fill that returns a size
recap.key: area(cell) = 1 + the areas of its unclaimed land neighbours. Claim before recursing. Keep the max over all floods.
recap.complexity: Time O(rows x cols). Space O(rows x cols).
moves: Make an owner grid, all empty
Scan for land with no owner
